newsitem.title: USA: AT&T cutting long-distance rates 5-15 pct.
newsitem.headline: AT&T cutting long-distance rates 5-15 pct.

text.p: AT&T Corp said Monday it will drop the basic rates for domestic long distance calls five percent during daytime and evening hours and 15 percent during night and weekend hours.

The company said this move comes as a result of a recent U.S. Federal Communications Commission order calling for reductions in the access fees long distance companies must pay to the monopoly local telephone companies.
AT&T said it is flowing through all the access reductions it receives, including a large share for consumers paying basic rates who do not subscribe to optional calling plans.

Under the current basic schedule, a 15-minute coast-to-coast direct-dialed call costs $4.65 during daytime hours, $2.85 during evening hours, and $2.40 during night/weekend hours. Beginning July 15, the same call will cost $4.35, $2.70 and $1.95, respectively.
The company said the rate reduction will affect AT&T customers who currently are not enrolled in a calling plan.
